rationale: Highest leverage among bounded candidates. parseCompoundStatementInternal is a single cohesive function (~260 lines) that owns the cursor loop for parsing compound statement bodies. It UNLOCKS_MULTIPLE_FOLLOWING_SURFACES (R1=1) because every statement, control-flow construct, declaration-inside-block, and nested compound eventually routes through this body parser; migrating it unblocks INV.PARSER.STMT (gated), parser/decl-in-block paths, and downstream const-eval reuse. Atomicity R2=1 (SMALL_COHESIVE_REGION) because the function has clear entry/exit, a single AST output parameter, and consumes the cursor token-by-token with explicit advance. Oracle R3=2 (EASY_BOUNDED_ORACLE) because the legacy C function is the entire authority and is observable through the resulting Ast + lexer state — a direct differential harness is achievable (same shape as lexer09-link-oracle). Dependency R4=2 (low) — direct deps are Cctrl *cc + body Ast + token loop; no external semantic region is touched. Proof R5=2 (bounded component + production seam) — same shape as LEXER04 fixedpoint. Span R6=260 (single function, less than parseToplevelDef+parseToAst which is the next-largest atomic slice).

Strong second-place. parseToplevelDef is a single dispatch loop with 5 inner branches; atomic slice exists. However, the body is a state-machine over the parser's lex token stream and depends on more parser-state coupling than parseCompoundStatementInternal (R4=3 vs 2). Proof cost R5=3 vs 2 because the production seam requires exercising parseToAst end-to-end (more stages of downstream consumers than compound). Span R6=460 (parseToplevelDef + parseToAst wrapper). Eligible but lower-ranked than INV.PARSER.COMPOUND.
